experiments.name: Extra order where the outcome looks settled
experiments.what: A second, separate order at the same price on markets where the nowcast puts YES under 20% (reliable hours) or the day's extreme is already locked (official 6-hour report, or weekend). Calm-clear-low nights are not logged live yet.
experiments.change: Doubles size only where spikes rarely come true. Needs free cash; on its own it can crowd out later fills at $2,000.
experiments.backtest: +$316 last 30 days, +$219 since Sep 11, placebo p 0.028; out-of-sample +$272 / +$303. Alone at $2k: about break-even (D131).
experiments.metric: Extra $ = the base order's $ again on flagged markets (assumes the extra order fills like the base).

headline.how: extra order repeats our $ on flagged markets

experiments.name: E1 plus cancel the extra order on one-sided buying
experiments.what: Same as E1, but the extra order is cancelled when the buying just before the spike is all one direction (someone who may know).
experiments.change: Keeps the good extra fills and skips the dangerous ones. Biggest single gain in the combined model (+$278/month model at $2k).
experiments.backtest: +$333 last 30 days, +$280 since Sep 11, 26.5¢ per extra contract, placebo p < 0.001.
experiments.metric: Extra $ = the base order's $ again on flagged, NOT one-sided markets.

headline.how: extra order repeats our $ on flagged, not one-sided markets

experiments.name: Pull the whole ladder on one-sided pre-spike buying (B1)
experiments.what: Cancel every rung when the buying in the minute before the spike is ≥96% YES and above 15¢.
experiments.change: Avoids the informed sweeps; costs the winners it also cancels. Market-wide history shows no effect, so it stays unproven.
experiments.backtest: +$155 to +$248 last 30 days out-of-sample on our fills, p 0.002; archive null.
experiments.metric: $ saved = minus bot B's $ on flagged markets (positive = pulling would have helped).

headline.how: $ saved by pulling flagged ladders (− = winners cut)
headline.exp_note: unproven — +$155 to +$248 last-30 on own fills, archive null

experiments.name: Fresh-reading window (pull 5–15 / 10–48 min after a new high/low reading)
experiments.what: Spikes that land 5–15 (or 10–48) minutes after a Wethr reading moved the day's extreme busted far more in the backtest — likely traders on 1-minute feeds acting before the public. Windows fixed in advance; live data decides.
experiments.change: If the window's YES rate stays well above outside, it becomes a pull rule (same websocket cancel as E2).
experiments.backtest: In-sample +$441 full / +$220 last 30 days; out-of-sample the best window moved (−$35). Mostly one Miami trade lately.
experiments.metric: YES rate of spikes in each window vs outside, on the tracker's burst population (any jump to ≥30¢ after an hour ≤15¢).

headline.how: $ saved by pulling our ladders in the windows
headline.exp_note: unproven out of sample — +$220 last-30 in-sample

experiments.name: Armed-market ceiling 150 → 200 (LIVE since 09-30 11:19 MT)
experiments.what: Raised to 200 on 09-30 at 11:19 MT. Counts spikes on markets the bot still skips at its limit (150 before the change, 200 after) — a measure of what a higher limit would still catch.
experiments.change: One number in the bot config. Settled-NO spikes here are wins a higher ceiling could have caught.
experiments.metric: Spikes on ceiling-skipped markets with no ladder resting; NO = missed win, YES = dodged bust.

headline.how: missed markets valued with the calibrated fill model on their real trades, at today's size (lows 100, highs 241); if every crossed rung had filled in full: +$30,126

experiments.name: Hourly temperature markets (Miami + NYC / Chicago / LA)
experiments.what: Same fade on the Synoptic-settled hourly markets. They settle on a regional index, so nobody can read the answer live. The LIVE hourly bot (since 10-02) runs the HOURLY_FULL rule at 1°F 10 / 2°F+ 20 ct — backtest $582/30d (RESULTS_REGISTRY §H); the model figure on this card is the original M30 rule at 50 ct.
experiments.change: Adds a new series family to the bot, with arming tuned for 60-minute markets. Miami first.
experiments.backtest: Miami +$24.60/day (CI +$7.24 to +$40.81), 71 markets, 5 busts, p < 0.001; ≈ +$375–450/month model — old M30 rule at 50 ct. The live bot's canonical number is $582/30d at 10/20 (D197/D199).
experiments.metric: YES rate of spikes to 30–60¢ after a quiet hour, by series (tracker definition, not the exact backtest arming rule).

headline.how: spikes valued with the calibrated fill model on their real trades, 4 rungs at 50 ct (the tested size)

experiments.name: A 25¢ rung (alternative form of extra size)
experiments.status: candidate — pick E1/E2 or this, not both
experiments.what: Spikes on markets where our ladder was resting that peaked at 25–29¢: a 25¢ rung would have filled, the 30¢ rung did not.
experiments.change: Extra contracts at a lower price. Same money as E1/E2 in a different shape.
experiments.metric: Near-miss spikes; NO = extra win at 25¢ (+25¢/ct), YES = extra bust (−75¢/ct).

headline.how: near-misses valued with the calibrated fill model: a 25¢ rung at our size (lows 100, highs 241)
headline.exp_note: +$340 last-30 (same money as E1/E2 — pick one)

experiments.name: 6¢ tail entry instead of 8¢
experiments.what: Splits bot B's filled markets by how quiet the tail was in the 2 hours before the spike.
experiments.change: Arming only after a ≤6¢ tail gives fewer, cleaner trades.
experiments.metric: Bust rate and $ of bot fills, ≤6¢ tail vs 7–8¢ tail.

headline.how: $ of our 7–8¢-tail markets a 6¢ rule would skip (sign flipped)

experiments.name: Lows capped at 100/rung (LIVE since 09-30 11:19 MT); highs above ~198 watched
experiments.what: Market-wide, extra contracts beyond these sizes lose (lows) or barely pay (highs). This tracks what OUR contracts above the line earn.
experiments.change: Lows capped at 100 per rung from 09-30 11:19 MT (orders already resting at 219 keep their size until they fill or re-arm). Highs keep growing with capital; this still watches highs above 198.
experiments.backtest: Market-wide: lows marginal ¢/ct −16 at 100→150; highs +4 at 198→250 (CI spans 0). Model: capping lows ≈ −$50–100/month avg, much better bad months.
experiments.metric: Realised $ of the contracts above the line, since the 09-19 size raise.

headline.how: capping lows at 100/rung forgoes the $ of contracts above 100

rule: Unsettled markets are scored PROVISIONALLY from the live price under TRACKING_RULES v1 rule 24: mid 50¢ or more → heading YES~, below → NO~. '~' marks provisional; they are never mixed into settled totals.
